note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

unit.title: Determine and plan for electrical installation requirements

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A client wants a new two-storey guest house in Treasure Beach wired. What should you settle first, to work out what the installation needs?
options: The brand of breakers the wholesaler has in stock this week
How each room will be used, the equipment planned and future plans
The colour of the switch and outlet cover plates in each guest room
Which electrician on the team lives closest to the guest house site

questions.stem: On a site survey for an extension to a shop, why do you look closely at the existing distribution board and main switch?
options: To choose a paint colour that matches the boards already in the shop
To find out how old the shop's building approval papers are
To see whether the shop owner has paid the last electricity bill
To find the spare ways, the main switch rating and their condition

questions.stem: A load assessment shows a new restaurant needs about 30 kW. Why is a 110 V-only supply not suitable?
options: The current at 110 V would be very high, so cables and service get huge
A 110 V supply cannot be used for any lights in a commercial kitchen
The power company bills restaurants on a 110 V supply only at night
A 110 V supply runs at a different frequency from a 220 V supply

questions.stem: The connected load for a large house is 24 kW. The design data gives a demand factor of 0.6. What maximum demand should be planned?
A house has a planned maximum demand of 13.2 kW, shared evenly across both lines of a 110/220 V supply. About what current flows in each line?
Why does a planner apply diversity, instead of adding up every connected load at its full rating?
options: Not all the loads run at full power at the same time
Diversity makes the cables run cooler in a hot roof space
The power company always asks for the smallest figure
It removes the need for any spare capacity on the board

questions.stem: A client plans to add a second floor to an office in about five years. What should the plan for the main board allow now?
options: A board that is exactly full, so no money is spent on unused ways
A second meter fitted now, ready for the new floor's first tenant
A smaller main cable now, to be changed when the floor is built
Spare ways, and a main cable and switch sized for the extra load

questions.stem: A design needs 30 circuits. The client's brief asks for at least 25% spare ways. What is the smallest number of ways the board must have?
A hotel has a pool deck with lights and outlets. Why is this area listed on its own in the installation requirements?
options: Pool areas take a different supply frequency from the rest of the hotel
Wet bodies and bare skin raise the shock risk, so more protection is needed
Pool lights must be wired by the pool builder, never by an electrician
The power company bills a pool area on its own separate meter

questions.stem: A new fish processing plant is being built beside the sea at Port Royal. Which requirement should the plan set for its electrical equipment?
options: Equipment painted white to reflect the strong sun
Indoor plastic boxes used for all the outdoor outlets
Corrosion-resistant enclosures with a suitable IP rating
Bare copper earth wires run along the outside walls

questions.stem: What should the requirements say about fixing outdoor A/C units and PV frames in an area that gets hurricanes?
options: Fixings rated for high wind, as the maker and the specification say
Units left loose, so they can be carried indoors before each storm
Light plastic brackets only, so the units break away in strong wind
No outdoor units at all, since storms come through every year

questions.stem: A client on a hilltop in Manchester has lost two TVs to lightning surges. What should the plan for the new installation include?
options: A larger main breaker, so it can carry the surge current
A 110 V supply in place of the 220 V supply to the house
Longer cable runs, so the cables soak up the surge energy
Surge protective devices, with good earthing and bonding

questions.stem: A small clinic needs its vaccine fridges and some lights to keep running in a power cut. How should the plan handle this?
options: Put every circuit in the clinic on the standby generator
Group the essential circuits on a board fed through a changeover
Plug the fridges into extension leads run from a neighbour
Leave it until after handover, when the clinic sees the need

questions.stem: In the requirements for a standby generator at a house, why is a changeover switch listed?
options: To stop the generator feeding back into the power company's lines
To let the generator and the mains share the house load equally
To make the generator start up much faster on a cool, damp morning
To let the meter run backwards whenever the generator is in use

questions.stem: Before promising a client a roof-mounted PV array, what must the planner check about the roof?
options: That its colour matches the colour of the panel frames
Its strength, direction, shading and the space it has
That it has a gutter on every side to drain the panels
That it is flat, because sloped roofs cannot hold panels

questions.stem: Why should the planner contact the power company early when a new building needs a large or three-phase supply?
options: The power company must design the building's lighting layout
The power company decides the size of every final circuit
The power company provides the cable for the inside wiring
The power company may need time to upgrade its line or transformer

questions.stem: Which document sets out the client's required standard of materials, workmanship and testing for an installation?
options: The supplier's delivery note
The job specification
The site diary for the job
The weekly timesheet

questions.stem: Before working out the requirements for a new office, which drawings should the planner get from the architect?
options: Floor plans with room uses, furniture layout and ceiling plans
The steel fabricator's shop drawings for the roof frame and nothing else
The landscape planting plan for the beds in the car park
The plumbing riser drawing for the water tanks on the roof

questions.stem: The client's brief asks for an ordinary outlet right beside the shower in a bathroom. What should the planner do?
options: Fit it as asked, because the client is paying for the job
Fit it, but leave the cover plate off so it can dry out
Explain the risk and offer a safe place the specification allows
Fit it at floor level so that the shower water cannot reach it

questions.stem: Which load list is the most useful for working out a building's maximum demand?
options: The client's list of the furniture and fittings in each room
The number of people expected to work in the building
The colour and the style of each light fitting chosen
Each item's rating, how many there are, and when it is used

questions.stem: A planned 2.2 kW A/C unit is expected to run 8 hours a day for 30 days. How many kWh is that in the month?
options: 264 kWh
528 kWh
660 kWh
17.6 kWh

questions.stem: A planned water heater will use 300 kWh a month. The tariff given is J$60 per kWh. What is the monthly energy cost, before GCT?
A client wants three A/C units added to an old house. The survey finds the main cable and switch are small and the board is full. What is the best plan?
options: Add the units to the existing outlet circuits to save money
Fit larger breakers on the old circuits so they do not trip
Plan a service and board upgrade, with the power company
Run extension leads from the board out to each A/C unit

questions.stem: An existing 100 A service has a measured maximum demand of 70 A. New loads will add 40 A. What should the planner conclude?
options: The service can take the new load with 10 A still to spare
The new loads should all go on one line to balance the board
The service is fine, because its breakers never trip now
The new total of 110 A is over the rating, so plan an upgrade

questions.stem: When planning new work in an occupied office, which requirement best protects the staff?
options: Working only at night with all the lights off to save energy
Barriers, planned shutdowns and isolation agreed with the client
Leaving the boards open so the staff can see the progress
Letting any staff member reset the breakers if anything trips

questions.stem: When planning resources for a large job, why list the test instruments and their calibration dates?
options: So calibrated instruments are on site when the tests are due
So the client can choose which brand of tester is used for each test
So the instruments can be hired out to the other trades
So the store can sell the oldest instruments first

questions.stem: Why must the planner know the delivery time of a large main switchboard early in the plan?
options: Large boards must be stored in the client's own office
The delivery time decides the cable colours for the job
A long-lead item can hold up the whole job if ordered late
The board's price falls when it is ordered at the last minute

questions.stem: Which list shows what an estimate for an installation should include?
options: Only the cost of the cable and the breakers
Only the labour hours at the normal hourly rate
The client's own costs for furniture and fittings
Materials, labour, plant, testing, overheads and GCT

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a room-by-room schedule of points (outlets, lights, data) agreed with the client?
options: It shows the electricians' working hours in each room
It records what each room needs, so nothing is missed
It lists the rooms that the painters will finish first
It replaces the need for any drawings on the job

questions.stem: A new office will have many computers. Which requirement should be added to the plan?
options: Enough circuits that the computers' normal leakage does not trip RCDs
One outlet circuit for the whole floor, to keep the wiring simple
Outlets at floor level only, because office desks are always low
Plain two-pin outlets, so that the computers are not earthed

questions.stem: Which building is most likely to need emergency escape lighting written into its requirements?
options: A small garden tool shed
A private car port at a house
A cinema with 200 seats
A storeroom in a private house

questions.stem: A planned workshop will have a large air compressor. What must the planner find out about it?
options: The colour of its tank, so it matches the walls
How loud its pump is when it runs at night
Who made its air hoses and quick-fit couplings
Its supply voltage, full-load and starting current

questions.stem: A client wants a pump 60 m from the house. Why is a 220 V pump better than a 110 V pump of the same power for this run?
options: A 220 V pump always runs faster than a 110 V pump
The current is half, so the volt drop is much lower
A 220 V pump does not need an earth conductor
Each kWh at 220 V costs less on the power bill

questions.stem: Where should the planner place the main switch of a new building?
options: Where it can be reached quickly and safely, near the supply entry
High up in the roof space, so that small children can never reach it
Inside a locked bedroom, so it is kept secure at all times
Behind the kitchen cupboards, so that it is out of sight

questions.stem: A warehouse with 9 m high racks needs good light in its aisles. Which detail should the requirements list?
options: The cheapest lamp, in the warmest colour
The same fittings used in the office upstairs
The light level needed and the mounting height
A light switch fixed at the end of every rack

questions.stem: A shop floor of 12 m by 10 m is to be lit at 8 W per square metre, as given in the design data. What lighting load should be planned?
A lighting load of 1 980 W at 110 V is to be split so that no circuit carries more than 10 A. What is the least number of circuits?
Why should the planner agree the main cable routes with the architect and the other trades at the planning stage?
options: To avoid clashes with ducts, pipes and beams before work starts
So the other trades can use the cables as a setting-out line
So the electricians can do their work in any order they like
So that the plumber pays a fair share of the cable used on the job

questions.stem: A client wants lower power bills in a new office. Which lighting choice in the plan helps most?
options: More lights than needed, all on one switch
Old fluorescent fittings taken from another job
LED fittings with daylight and occupancy sensors
All the lights on a timer that runs the whole day

questions.stem: Why should the planner ask about ground conditions early on a rocky hillside site?
options: Rocky ground makes the cables run hotter in summer
Rocky ground changes the frequency of the supply
Rocky ground means that no earthing is needed
A low earth resistance may be hard to get there

questions.stem: After writing up the requirements, why does the planner ask the client to sign them?
options: So the planner can stop taking the client's phone calls
So both sides agree the scope before design and pricing
So the client pays the full price before work starts
So the power company can connect the supply sooner

questions.stem: Which item is NOT normally part of working out an installation's requirements?
options: Choosing the electricians' lunch break times
Listing the loads and how they will be used
Checking what supply is available at the site
Noting special locations and the environment

questions.stem: Halfway through planning, the client adds a commercial kitchen to the ground floor. What should the planner do?
options: Keep the old load figures, since the plan is half done
Add the kitchen loads to an existing outlet circuit
Update the load, supply needs, cost and programme
Tell the client a kitchen can be added only after handover

questions.stem: You are leading two trainees on a site survey. Which task is best to give them?
options: Deciding the size of the new service on their own
Agreeing the final price of the job with the client
Signing the requirements on behalf of the firm
Measuring rooms and recording the existing points

questions.stem: A hotel wants outlets at its outdoor beach bar. Which requirement fits best?
options: Ordinary indoor outlets, fixed under the bar counter
Weatherproof outlets with RCD (GFCI) protection
Outlets on long flexible cords from the kitchen
Outlets set into the sand so they are out of sight

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the term for the largest load a building is expected to draw at one time, used to size its supply?
What is the term for the total of the ratings of every load installed in a building, before diversity is applied?
What do we call an item that takes a long time to deliver, such as a large switchboard, and so must be ordered early?
What is the client's written statement called that says what they want the installation to do, before any design starts?
What is the visit to a site called, made to record the existing conditions before the requirements are written?
A design needs 120 m of cable, and the planner adds 10% for waste and terminations. How many metres should be ordered?
How many volts are there between the two line conductors of a Jamaican 110/220 V split-phase supply?
The specification limits the volt drop on a 220 V A/C circuit to 4%. How many volts is that?
What term describes the extra capacity left on a board or a service for loads that will be added later?
In Jamaica, which direction should fixed PV panels generally face to collect the most sun over the year? (one word)
Which two-letter code on an enclosure shows how well it keeps out dust and water?
Name the type of supply with three line conductors, used for large motors and large buildings.
What word describes a load, such as a vaccine fridge or a fire pump, that must keep running during a power cut?
Which problem, common near Jamaica's coast, eats away metal enclosures, fixings and terminals?
What is the list of materials and their quantities, counted and measured from the drawings, usually called?

essays.stem: You are asked to find out what a client needs for the electrical installation of a new small hotel in Negril. Describe how you would gather, record and agree the client's requirements.
essays.modelAnswer: I would arrange a meeting with the client and, if possible, the architect, and use a checklist so nothing is missed. I would ask how each area will be used: guest rooms, kitchen, laundry, bar, pool, offices and outside areas. I would list the equipment planned, such as A/C units, water heaters, kitchen equipment, pumps, lifts and data systems, and ask for the makers' data. I would ask which loads must keep running in a power cut, whether solar PV is wanted, and what growth is planned in the next few years. I would also ask about the budget, the opening date and any standards the client or the owners' brand requires. I would get the drawings, then visit the site to see the supply, the ground and the sea air. I would write everything up as a room-by-room schedule and a list of special needs, send it to the client, answer their questions, and get it signed before the design and pricing start.
markingPoints: Meets the client (and architect) and uses a checklist
Finds the use of each area and the equipment planned, with makers' data
Asks about standby needs, solar, future growth, budget and dates
Gets drawings and visits the site
Writes the requirements up and has the client agree and sign them

essays.stem: Explain how you would carry out a load assessment for a new house with A/C units, a water heater, a stove, a pump, lighting and outlets. Say how you would use the result to decide the supply.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would list every load with its rating, from the nameplate or the maker's data: for example three A/C units, the water heater, the stove, the pump, the lighting and the outlet circuits. I would note whether each runs at 110 V or 220 V, and how long and when it is used. Adding all the ratings gives the connected load. Not everything runs at full power together, so I would apply the diversity or demand factors given in the design data or the specification, to get the maximum demand. I would also add an allowance for future loads the client has mentioned. The maximum demand in watts, divided by 220 V for a balanced split-phase supply, gives the current in each line. From that I would choose the size of the service, the main switch and the main cable, and check with the power company that its supply can carry it. I would also share the loads evenly between the two lines.
markingPoints: Lists each load with its rating, voltage and pattern of use
Adds the ratings to get the connected load
Applies the given diversity or demand factors to find maximum demand
Allows for future loads
Works out the line current and uses it to size the service, main switch and cable, with the power company's agreement

essays.stem: Describe what you would check and record on a site survey before planning an extension to an existing shop installation.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the visit I would ask for any drawings, test records and recent bills. On site I would look at the supply: the meter, the service cable, the main switch rating and its condition. I would check the distribution board for spare ways, its make and age, overheating marks and labelling. I would look at the earthing and bonding and note the earth rod if I can find it. I would note the wiring type and its age, and any signs of damage or poor work. I would measure the rooms where the extension will go, find routes for new cables, and note walls, ceilings, beams and other services in the way. I would ask the owner about trips and faults, and when work can be done without stopping trade. I would take photos and notes on a survey sheet, mark them on a floor plan, and record anything unsafe so it can be reported to the owner straight away.
markingPoints: Collects existing drawings, records and bills
Checks the supply, main switch and board (spare ways, condition, labels)
Checks earthing, bonding and the condition of existing wiring
Measures the area and plans cable routes, noting obstacles
Records with photos and notes, asks the owner, and reports anything unsafe

essays.stem: Explain how Jamaica's environment (salt air, heat, hurricanes, lightning and flooding) affects the requirements you set for an installation. Give an example for each.
essays.modelAnswer: Near the coast, salt air corrodes metal, so I would ask for enclosures, fixings and glands that resist corrosion, with a suitable IP rating, for example on a seaside hotel's outdoor lights. Heat affects cables: in a hot roof space a cable carries less current, so the requirements must say where cables run so they can be derated, and A/C loads will be large. Hurricanes bring strong winds, so outdoor A/C units, PV frames and service masts need fixings rated for wind as the maker says, and a standby supply may be needed. Lightning is common in the hills, so I would ask for surge protective devices at the main board and near sensitive equipment, with good earthing and bonding. Flooding happens in low areas such as parts of Old Harbour, so the main board, meter and outlets should be placed above the likely flood level. Writing these into the requirements early means the design and the price allow for them.
markingPoints: Salt air: corrosion-resistant equipment and suitable IP rating
Heat: derating of cables and larger cooling loads
Hurricanes: wind-rated fixings and possibly standby supply
Lightning: surge protection with good earthing and bonding
Flooding: equipment placed above flood level; set early so design and price allow for it

essays.stem: A health centre in May Pen wants some services to keep running during power cuts. Explain how you would work out its standby power requirements.
essays.modelAnswer: I would sit with the centre's manager and list which loads are essential: for example the vaccine fridges, some lighting, the emergency lighting, the nurses' station outlets, the computer server and perhaps one A/C unit. I would find each load's rating and starting current, and work out the essential maximum demand with the diversity in the design data. That sets the size of the generator, with a margin for motor starting and future needs. I would plan to group the essential circuits on their own board, fed through a changeover switch so the generator can never feed back into the power company's lines. I would ask how long the centre must run in a long outage, to size the fuel tank, and whether loads that cannot stand even a short break, such as the server, need a UPS. I would also note where the generator can stand, with ventilation, noise and fuel safety, and add all this to the requirements for the client to agree.
markingPoints: Lists the essential loads with the client
Works out the essential demand, allowing for starting current and growth
Plans an essential board fed through a changeover switch to stop back-feed
Considers run time and fuel, and a UPS for loads that cannot have a break
Considers the generator's position and safety, and gets the client's agreement

essays.stem: Explain which approvals and outside bodies you must plan for when setting the requirements for a new commercial building, and why each must be built into the plan early.
essays.modelAnswer: The power company must be contacted early with the expected load, because it decides the type of supply it can give, where the service and meter will go, and whether its line or transformer needs upgrading, which can take weeks or months. Its paperwork must be in order before it connects. The government electrical inspection must be planned, because the inspector must pass the installation before the power company will connect it, so the programme needs time for the visit and for any corrections. The building's planning approval from the local authority affects where the service, the meter and the generator can go. If grid-tied solar is wanted, the power company's own approval and checks are needed before any power is exported. The client's insurer, the fire service or a brand standard may add requirements such as fire alarms and emergency lighting. Building these in early avoids delays at the end and avoids rework when an approval asks for changes.
markingPoints: Power company: early notice of the load, supply type, service position and possible upgrade
Government electrical inspection before connection, with time in the programme
Local authority building approval affecting positions
Power company approval for grid-tied PV
Explains that early planning avoids delays and rework

essays.stem: Compare a 110 V-only supply, a 110/220 V split-phase supply and a three-phase supply. Say which kinds of building each suits and why.
essays.modelAnswer: A 110 V-only supply has one line and a neutral. It suits a very small home or a small shop with only lights, outlets and small appliances. Large loads draw high currents at 110 V, so it cannot sensibly feed big A/C units, stoves or water heaters. A 110/220 V split-phase supply has two lines and a neutral: each line is 110 V to neutral and the two lines give 220 V between them. It suits most Jamaican homes and many small businesses, because lights and outlets run at 110 V, while A/C units, stoves and water heaters run at 220 V and draw half the current they would at 110 V. A three-phase supply has three lines. It suits factories, hotels, malls and large offices, because it carries large loads with smaller cables and runs three-phase motors, such as pumps, compressors and lifts, which start and run smoothly. The planner chooses from the load assessment and what the power company can supply.
markingPoints: 110 V-only: small loads only, high current for large loads
Split-phase: two lines, 110 V and 220 V, suits most homes and small businesses
Explains that 220 V loads draw half the current of the same power at 110 V
Three-phase: large buildings and three-phase motors, smaller cables for large loads
Choice made from the load assessment and the power company's supply

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare a cost estimate for the installation requirements of a new office, so the client can approve a budget.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start from the agreed requirements, the drawings and the schedule of points. I would do a take-off: counting outlets, lights, boards, switches and equipment, and measuring cable and containment runs, with an allowance for waste. I would price the materials from current supplier quotes. For labour, I would estimate the hours for each part of the work from past jobs, and multiply by the hourly rates. I would add plant and equipment hire, such as scaffolds or a lift, the testing and commissioning time, the inspection and power company fees, transport, and the firm's overheads and profit. I would add a contingency for unknowns, and then GCT at the current rate. I would list what is included and what is not, such as builder's work or the A/C units themselves, and state how long the prices hold. The estimate goes to the client with the assumptions clearly written, so any change can be priced fairly.
markingPoints: Starts from the agreed requirements and does a take-off of quantities
Prices materials from current quotes and labour from estimated hours
Adds plant, testing, fees, overheads and profit
Adds contingency and GCT at the current rate
States inclusions, exclusions, assumptions and how long prices hold

essays.stem: Explain how you would plan the resources and the programme for installing a new building's electrical services, and how you would supervise the team.
essays.modelAnswer: From the requirements I would break the job into stages: containment and first fix, boards and sub-mains, second fix, testing, inspection and connection. For each stage I would estimate the labour hours and decide how many electricians and helpers are needed and when, fitting in with the builder's programme. I would order long-lead items, such as the main switchboard and the generator, early, and plan deliveries so materials arrive when needed and can be stored safely. I would list the plant and tools, such as access equipment, cable pulling gear and calibrated test instruments. I would allow time for the government inspection and the power company. To supervise, I would brief the team each morning on tasks and safety, give clear job cards, check work at set stages before it is covered, and record progress against the programme so any delay is seen early and dealt with.
markingPoints: Breaks the job into stages and estimates labour for each
Plans team size and timing with the builder's programme
Orders long-lead items early and plans deliveries and storage
Lists plant, tools and calibrated instruments, and allows for inspection and connection
Supervises with briefings, job cards, stage checks and progress tracking

essays.stem: Explain why installation requirements must be written down and agreed with the client, and how you would handle a change the client asks for later.
essays.modelAnswer: Written requirements make sure the client and the contractor mean the same thing. They set the scope for the design and the price, so the estimate is fair and complete. They give the designer and the team a clear target, and they settle arguments later about what was promised. If the client signs them, both sides have a record. When the client asks for a change, such as more outlets or a new kitchen, I would write down the request and confirm it with them. Then I would check what it affects: the load assessment, the supply and board size, the cables, the cost and the programme. I would send the client a written variation with the extra cost and time, and wait for their written approval before the team does the work. Then I would update the requirements, drawings and programme so everyone works from the same version.
markingPoints: Written requirements set a shared, clear scope for design and price
A signed record settles later disputes
Records and confirms the change request
Checks the effect on load, supply, cost and programme, and prices it as a variation
Gets written approval first, then updates the documents

practical1.title: Survey a training block and write its installation requirements
practical1.brief: The group surveys a part of the Centre chosen by the assessor (for example a classroom block or workshop) as if it were to be rewired and extended. The installation stays in normal use: no covers are removed and no boards are opened by trainees; the assessor opens the board for viewing with its circuits isolated if the Centre's rules allow. Give each member a role (team leader, two surveyors, load recorder, and client liaison) and swap so everyone measures and records. Interview the assessor, who plays the client, about the planned use of each room, new equipment and future growth. Measure each room, record the existing points on a survey sheet, and mark them on a floor plan. List the loads with their ratings, and work out the connected load and the maximum demand using the demand factors the assessor gives. Note the supply, the board's spare ways, the environment and any special locations. Write a room-by-room schedule of requirements and a one-page summary for the client to sign.
materials: Access to a part of the Centre chosen by the assessor
Floor plan outline (or squared paper) and survey sheets
Laser distance meter and measuring tape
Assessor's sheet of demand factors and planned new equipment
Blank schedule of requirements and summary forms
photos: The interview with the client (assessor), with the notes taken
Members measuring a room with the laser meter and tape
The floor plan marked with existing points
The load list with the connected load and maximum demand worked out
The signed summary for the client
checklist: Asked the client clear questions about use, equipment and future growth
Measured rooms accurately and recorded existing points correctly
Listed loads with ratings and worked out the maximum demand correctly
Noted the supply, spare ways, environment and special locations
Wrote part of the schedule of requirements clearly
Kept to the rule of not opening any live equipment
Worked well in the team and swapped roles as planned
safety: Do not remove covers or open boards: the survey is visual only, and only the assessor opens a board with its circuits isolated
Use a stable step or ladder only if one is needed, with a member footing it
Keep walkways clear and do not disturb people working in the area
Report anything unsafe you see, such as a damaged outlet, to the assessor at once

practical2.title: Plan the requirements for a new clinic from a client brief
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a made-up brief and floor plans for a new single-storey clinic in Mandeville: consulting rooms, a pharmacy store with vaccine fridges, a waiting area, offices, toilets, a small server room and an outside car park. As a group, give each member a role (lead planner, load assessor, standby and special-areas planner, approvals and programme planner, and estimator) and swap checks so everyone reviews another member's work. Produce: a load list with the connected load and maximum demand (using the assessor's demand factors), the supply choice with reasons, the number of board ways with 25% spare, a list of essential loads for a standby generator with a changeover switch, the special locations and environmental needs, a list of approvals and outside bodies with when to contact them, a simple programme, and an outline cost estimate using the assessor's prices with GCT at the current rate. Then present the plan to the assessor, who plays the clinic's manager, and answer questions.
materials: Made-up client brief and floor plans for a clinic
Assessor's sheet of equipment ratings, demand factors and unit prices
Calculators, rulers, coloured pens and A3 paper
Blank load list, requirements schedule and estimate forms
Flip chart or whiteboard for the presentation
photos: The load list with connected load and maximum demand
The marked-up floor plan showing special locations and the essential circuits
The supply choice and board ways worked out
The presentation to the client, with the flip chart
